Fine, whatever. If I were just practicing, how would I even find a capital letter in a string using Python?

That is a great general question. In Python, strings have a built-in method called `.isupper()` which returns True if a character is an uppercase letter. For example, if you have a character `char`, you can check it using `if char.isupper():`. This is very useful when you are looping through a string to analyze each character.
Okay, and if I wanted to put a space before that capital letter, how would I do that in a new string?

A common approach is to create an empty string and then append characters to it one by one. If you encounter a character that meets your criteria (like being uppercase), you can append a space to your new string first, and then append the character itself. This allows you to build the modified version of the text step-by-step.
